bib.title: STaR: Self-Taught Reasoner. Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning

read.skipped: Appendix C human-eval example lists and Appendix D/A examples were skimmed (illustrative rationales only).

question: Can a pretrained LLM bootstrap its own rationale-generation ability from a few rationale examples plus a large dataset of question-answer pairs without rationales?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning on self-generated rationales that reach the correct answer, plus rationalization of failed problems with the answer as hint, iteratively improves reasoning.
contributions: A bootstrapping mechanism to iteratively generate a rationale dataset from a few initial examples, without checking rationale correctness.
Rationalization: justify a given answer, then fine-tune as if no hint was given; it accelerates and improves bootstrapping.
Evaluation with ablations on mathematical and commonsense reasoning.
First technique to let a pretrained LLM iteratively use its language modeling capacity to improve itself (authors' claim).

method.summary: Few-shot prompt GPT-J to generate rationale+answer for each training question, keep rationales whose answer matches ground truth, rationalize failures by giving the answer as a hint, then fine-tune the original pretrained model on the union and repeat for N outer iterations.
method.task: rationale-augmented reasoning: n-digit addition with scratchpads, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K

datasets.name: Arithmetic (n-digit addition, 1-5 digits, Nye et al. scratchpad format)
datasets.size: 50,000 generated questions; 10,000 sampled per outer iteration
datasets.preprocessing: 10 random few-shot rationale examples per digit length

datasets.name: CommonsenseQA (CQA)
datasets.size: 12,247 questions, 5 choices each: 9,741 train, 1,221 dev, 1,285 test (withheld)
datasets.split: train for STaR, dev accuracy reported
datasets.source: Talmor et al. 2019, built from ConceptNet
datasets.preprocessing: 10 few-shot prompts from Wei et al. with rationales modified to fix an incorrect answer and reference knowledge more explicitly

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.preprocessing: few-shot prompt of 6 examples in Appendix I

models.name: GPT-J
models.init_from: pretrained on the Pile; each outer iteration fine-tunes from the original pretrained model, not the previous iteration

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning (next-token) on filtered self-generated rationales; framed as approximate policy gradient with indicator reward 1(y_hat = y)
training.steps: 40 at first outer loop, +20% per outer loop (arithmetic with rationalization: 300 initial, +20 per iteration; GSM8K capped at 7912 steps from 30th iteration)
training.regularisation: retrain from the original pretrained model each iteration to avoid overfitting

other.outer_iterations: arithmetic 16 (Fig 4 text); GSM8K 36 iterations without rationalization plus 10 with; run until performance saturates, best reported
other.few_shot_in_finetuning: few-shot prompts included during fine-tuning in the main setup

inference.decoding: greedy decoding of rationale and answer (Sec 3.1); outputs from a 'low sampling temperature' (Sec 5)
inference.temperature: low/greedy; 0.5 and 0.7 tried as an alternative to rationalization and were worse
inference.samples: one sample per question per iteration
inference.prompting: few-shot (10 rationale examples for CQA and per arithmetic digit length; 6 for GSM8K); rationalization adds the correct answer as a hint, removed from the training prompt

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of correct final answers (CQA dev, GSM8K test, n-digit arithmetic)

eval.protocol: single reported run, best iteration reported; no seeds or confidence intervals; human ranking study: 20 Prolific crowdworkers, 10 questions each from 50 questions

prompts.text:
Q: Where do you put your grapes just before checking out?
Answer Choices:
(a) mouth
(b) grocery cart (CORRECT)
(c) super market
(d) fruit basket
(e) fruit market
A: The answer should be the place where grocery items are placed before checking out. Of the above choices, grocery cart makes the most sense for holding grocery items. Therefore, the answer is grocery cart (b).

results.claim: GPT-2 could not bootstrap from few-shot reasoning even on arithmetic.
results.quote: GPT-2 was not able to bootstrap from few-shot reasoning in even the arithmetic domain

limits: Initial few-shot performance must be above chance; GPT-2 failed to bootstrap on arithmetic.
Tasks with high chance performance (binary decisions) yield many poor rationales; filtering them is open.
Single base model (GPT-J 6B); no seeds or variance; hyperparameter search was limited by compute.
Rationale quality on CQA judged qualitatively and by a small preliminary human study.
Rationalization needs a hint that may not follow from question and answer in other domains.
Amplifies dataset biases and does not ensure rationale faithfulness (Appendix G).
Rationalization gave little gain on GSM8K (10.1 to 10.7).
